$comment: TD-171 AC3: THE canonical story-lifecycle status vocabulary , the single definition point consumed by BOTH kits/core/skills/backlog-management/scripts/user-story-validator.py and kits/core/tools/pipeline_validator.py (each resolves this file relative to its own location, an offset invariant across the kits/core, .opencode and .claude layouts). Do not add spellings here to silence a validator: the 2026-05..07 audit drift (TD-171 Group B) was expressible precisely because the old 18-value set admitted 'active'/'done'/'completed' into story frontmatter. GTD/kanban TODO-note statuses (todo, pending, scheduled, ...) are a DIFFERENT vocabulary for Obsidian TODO notes and never belong in story frontmatter.
$quality_gate_comment: BUG-004: the canonical QUALITY-GATE status vocabulary, consumed by pipeline_validator.py's _check_quality_gates_pass. Three CLASSES, not a flat list, because a gate has three meaningful outcomes: it passed, it did not apply, or it did not pass. Anything NOT listed here FAILS (fail-closed) , that is the whole point of BUG-004, whose defect was a vacuous all([]) reporting green while never reading a status. WHY ALIASES ARE HERE AND WHY THIS IS NOT THE DRIFT THE story_status COMMENT WARNS AGAINST: that warning is about TIGHTENING a vocabulary for records written GOING FORWARD, where extra spellings ADMIT BAD STATES. This key must READ 177 records ALREADY WRITTEN, over a period when no gate vocabulary existed at all , 1,015 entries across 11 spellings. The aliases are a COMPATIBILITY LAYER over historical data, not a loosening of a live contract: they let the checker classify the past without lying about it. NEW records SHOULD write the canonical first spelling of each class ('pass', 'not_applicable', 'fail'). Do NOT add a spelling here to silence a red gate , that is exactly the failure this file exists to prevent.
